content.title: Are You Taking Away Your Child's Childhood?
content.subtitle: Your child needs your time, not your screen.
content.body:
Did you know? Spending more than 2 hours a day on screens can reduce your child's ability to learn new things by up to 47%.

According to multiple reports published in JAMA Pediatrics, when parents excessively use their phones in front of their children, it can reduce children's language development and emotional regulation. It is also associated with nearly a 40% increase in behavioral problems such as irritability, stubbornness, and hyperactivity.

Psychological Neglect of Children

Psychologists call this "Technoference"—the unwanted interference of technology in human relationships. Children are natural imitators. They learn about the world through their parents' smiles, attention, and affection. When they repeatedly find a lifeless phone instead of a caring face, their social and emotional development begins to suffer.

The Cost of Imitation: The Alarming Reality of Children's Screen Addiction

As children imitate their parents, they too become addicted to screens. Global research shows that excessive screen time can reduce children's attention span by up to 73%. It also increases the risk of anxiety and emotional distress by 61%. Spending more than 2 hours a day on screens can impair their language and learning abilities by up to 47%, while doubling the risk of loneliness and depression later in life.

The Pull of the Virtual World vs. Real Parenting

Your child doesn't ask for expensive toys; they need your presence and undivided attention. While you're absorbed in YouTube or other digital platforms, your child may be spending the most valuable moments of childhood alone. This emotional distance can gradually lead to social withdrawal.

Let Awareness Begin Today

Parents are the builders of the next generation. Help your children grow with strong moral values and emotional well-being. Remember, a little awareness today can make your child's future brighter.
